text:
Anaheim arrives in Edmonton on a high, though a shaky one: the Ducks beat Vancouver 5-4 on Tuesday behind a three-goal night from Cutter Gauthier, and they're 3-1-1 in their last five without A.J. Greer and Ryan Poehling. Edmonton's three-game winning streak ended in a 4-3 shootout loss at New Jersey, and the Oilers are missing Zach Hyman (neck) and Isaac Howard. This is also a rematch of last spring's first-round series, which the Ducks won in six games. Edmonton won the first meeting this season 5-2.

Our numbers lean slightly toward the Oilers (3.24 expected goals to 2.95, a measure of chance quality). Anaheim has taken just 44% of the expected goals at five on five and allows 3.48 per 60 minutes. Edmonton's results run ahead of its chances, so we'd treat the +20 goal difference with some caution. The special-teams matchup to watch pits Edmonton's power play (0.88 expected goals a game) against a Ducks penalty kill allowing 0.82, and Anaheim takes 5.1 penalties a game. In net, Lukas Dostal (projected) sits at +0.3 goals saved above expected this season, a measure of how many goals he's stopped beyond what the shots called for, but was at -3.7 last year. Tristan Jarry (projected) is at -1.7 this season and -4.2 last.

Gauthier, who has scored in three straight, is 41% to score for us, and Leo Carlsson is 74% for a point. For Edmonton, Leon Draisaitl is 46% to score and Connor McDavid, on a 16-game point streak, is 93% for a point. Among our under-the-radar picks: Kasperi Kapanen, now at 19:46 a night with Hyman out, is 46% for a point, and fourth-liner Filip Hallander has been dangerous in limited minutes. Both are players to watch, not locks.
